svg.title: Aggregated engine steps mix prefill chunks into decode steps; P/D keeps decode steps short but queues prefill
svg.desc: Top lane: one aggregated TP8+EP8 engine at 256 sessions, FP8 KV. Many steps carry a prefill chunk of up to 8,192 tokens next to the running decodes, so the time between tokens stretches. Lower lanes: P/D with 4 prefill GPUs and 4 decode GPUs; decode steps carry only decodes while the prefill queue grows. Measured end to end: aggregated TTFT p90 4.10 s, ITL p90 56.4 ms, 16.08 req/s; P/D TTFT p90 44.4 s, ITL p90 38.5 ms, 6.70 req/s.
svg.text: Why P/D steadies streaming but stretches time to first token (256 sessions, FP8 KV)
Each box is one engine step; every running request gets one token per step, so a longer step means a longer gap between tokens
prefill chunk (up to 8,192 prompt tokens per step)
KV hand-off over NVLink: 35 ms per transfer here (17 ms at 64 sessions), measured per stage
Measured end to end (client side, whole request):
Aggregated: TTFT p90 4.10 s, ITL p90 56.4 ms (over the 50 ms SLO), 402 output tok/s/GPU
P/D 1P:1D: TTFT p90 44.4 s (lower bound, run hit its time cap), ITL p90 38.5 ms, 167 output tok/s/GPU
Box widths are schematic; only the numbers are measured. Both runs FP8 KV; the only change is the topology. Single runs.
Qwen3-235B-A22B-Instruct-2507 FP8 | 8x H100 SXM5 | Dynamo 1.6.0 + vLLM 0.31.0 | NIXL 1.4.1
